Self-Evolving Extraction · Final Record

抽取策略进化志

离线内容库网页字段抽取（标题、正文、作者、发布时间、更新时间）的算法链路自进化全记录：从 v4 规则基线到 v15「规则管线优先 + 门控模型补全」的最终方案，共 11 轮经 git 版本化的迭代，覆盖三套数据集与两条成本曲线。

dev 模型补全层触发率——模型成本只落在规则失陷页
规则管线
由站点规则库、元数据解析、trafilatura 通用引擎与 DOM 密度回退构成的确定性抽取链路，单页耗时约 85 毫秒，无外部依赖。
模型补全层
规则管线输出低置信时方才触发的本地大模型补全过程（Qwen2.5-7B，约 2 秒/页）；其输出必须通过页内证据核验方可采纳，否则弃用并回退规则结果。
触发门控
决定单页是否调用模型的判定逻辑：仅当标题缺失或来源过弱、作者为空、发布时间为空，且未被规则层终判为「本站无此字段」时触发。
规则层终判
规则管线对特定站点给出的「该字段不存在」的确定性结论；一经终判，模型补全层同样禁止回填该字段。
误填 / 漏填
误填（false fill）：标注为空而系统给出了值；漏填（miss）：标注有值而系统为空。本方案将误填视为比漏填更严重的事故。
口径挂起项
系统输出与标注答案不一致、但争议点在标注规范本身的条目；登记挂起、不为此修改标注，也不计入策略缺陷。
ISPRAS 基准
俄罗斯科学院系统编程研究所（ISPRAS）公开的英文新闻网页抽取评测集，本项目取 160 页 / 80 站作为跨语言外部基准。
01 · Field Contract

字段契约：下游使用说明

输出为逐页一条 JSON 记录。下表为字段类型与语义约定；其后的使用要点面向接入方——哪些断言可以依赖、哪些需要自己裁决。完整的输入输出实例见 §07。

字段类型语义与约定空值语义
titlestring | null文章真实标题；站点后缀、栏目链已剥离（中文 -- 链 / 英文品牌段）null = 未检出
authorsstring[] | null署名作者（含机构署名），多人按页面出现顺序；已过媒体名 / 社媒词 / 敬称 / 机构角色过滤null = 页面无署名或未检出
publish_time
update_time		object | null{value, utc_offset, utc_offset_source}；value 固定 YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS 形，未知位以 XX 占位（如 2024-03-11 XX:XX:XX 表示仅知日期）null = 未检出或规则层终判本站无此字段
content_textstring纯文本正文；图片以 [[IMG_n]] 占位，与 images[n] 一一对应（图说在 images[n].caption）；Markdown 形态见 content_md拒识页为 null
rejectedbooleantrue = 系统判定该页无可抽取正文（列表页 / 图集 / 空壳），全部字段为空，原因见 provenance.refusal—
provenanceobject逐字段出处标记：dom://… 站点规则、meta:/json-ld: 元数据、trafilatura:… 通用引擎、model:qwen2.5-7b(verified:…) 模型补全（已通过页内核验）、refusal 拒识理由—

接入要点

  1. 空值语义不区分「页面确实没有」与「系统没抽到」。需要区分时查 provenance：带规则层终判标记的字段属于前者；其余 null 视为「低置信留空」。
  2. 时间比较按公共精度截断：value 中的 XX 为未知位，下游做相等性判断或排序时应按非 XX 前缀截断（与评分口径一致）。utc_offset 可能为 null（页面未给时区）；utc_offset_source = inferred_site_locale 表示时区按站点地区推断、并非页面显式给出——跨时区聚合时需留意。
  3. 全方案按「宁缺勿滥」调校：test 集误填三项全部为 0。字段为 null 更可能是「谨慎不答」而非「漏看」；若下游宁可多不可缺，可在重标定后开启宽松模式（涉及拒识与时间字段的判定阈值）。
  4. 拒识记录应跳过或走双轨：rejected=true 不产出任何字段。注意任务定义分歧——部分上游（如 ISPRAS）把专题聚合页列为抽取对象；如下游需要，可改为「拒识标记 + 尽力而为字段」双轨输出。
  5. 模型产出可识别、可剥离：provenance 以 model: 前缀标记模型补全层产出（均已通过页内核验链）。对来源敏感的下游可按来源过滤——只采信规则与元数据来源的字段，退化为纯规则方案。
  6. 作者为署名原文：保留「（摄影）」「（责任编辑）」等角色后缀与机构署名原文；角色结构化（摄影 / 执笔 / 责编分列）属于下游归一化的职责，本层不做。
02 · Evaluation & Metrics

评测设计与指标定义

数据集分工

  • dev 固定子集 30 页：3 个规则站点各 10 页——规则库回归基准
  • dev 通用子集 55 页：11 个通用站点各 5 页——策略调优的唯一依据
  • dev 拒识负例 4 页：频道列表页——拒识判定的负例
  • test 预留集 28 页：模板隔离（gmw 站点族，含 8 个应拒识图集页）——交付时一次性评测，只读聚合结果
  • ISPRAS 外部基准 160 页：80 个英文站点——跨语言泛化验证，不参与调优

评测纪律（全程未破）

  • 调优只看 dev；test 全程仅在交付时做一次聚合评测
  • 评分器冻结（49 项单元测试护住口径，任何修改即失败）
  • 标注答案不为分数回改——边界争议登记为口径挂起项（cnblogs 共 11 项）
  • 每轮全量重评 + 逐页差异比对；出现回归即修复或整体回滚
  • 模型输出必须页内可核验——从机制上杜绝编造通道

指标公式定义

设评测页集 𝒫 = {p₁, …, pN}，单页得分 s(p) ∈ [0,1]，主指标均为宏平均：

S = (1/N) · Σp∈𝒫 s(p)

除「正确判空」外，失败样本永不离开分母：标注为空的页面，系统同样答空方得 1 分，答错记 0 分——防止「空页面一律留空」或「一律猜值」两类投机。

① 标题（精确匹配率）

stitle(p) = 1[ ν(t̂) = ν(t*) ]

t̂ 为系统输出，t* 为标注答案；ν 为规范化函数（去除空白、大小写折叠、全半角归一化）。另有诊断量 title_sim（归一化编辑相似度）用于区分「完全不符」与「后缀型偏差」，仅作分析、不计入总分。

② 作者（集合 F1）

P = |Â ∩ A*| / |Â|    R = |Â ∩ A*| / |A*|    sauthors(p) = 2PR / (P + R)

A* 为标注作者集合，Â 为预测集合；A* 为空且 Â 为空时记 1 分。配套分解指标：误填率（标注为空而预测非空的页面占比）与漏填率（反之）——本方案将误填视为头等事故，生产环境中填错作者比漏填更损害可信度。

③ 时间（按标注精度截断比较）

stime(p) = 1[ trunc(t̂, g) = trunc(t*, g) ],  g ∈ {年, 月, 日, 时, 分, 秒}

g 取标注答案自身的精度：标注精确到日则只比较日期部分，避免「系统多给了时分」反而失分。发布时间与更新时间分别计分，另维护两者的混淆矩阵与时区三态（一致 / 缺失 / 冲突）作为诊断。

④ 正文（字符 3-gram 多重集 F1）

P = Σk min(M̂k, M*k) / Σk M̂k    R = Σk min(M̂k, M*k) / Σk M*k    scontent(p) = 2PR / (P + R)

M̂、M* 分别为预测与标注正文的字符 3-gram 多重集（保留重复计数，对「同一句复制两遍」敏感）。诊断量：LCS-F1（保序程度）、dup_ratio（重复率）、num_f1（数字保真度）、para_ratio（段落结构比）。

⑤ 拒识（互斥分母的拒识准确率）

Acc⁺ = |{p ∈ 𝒫⁺ : 系统拒识 p}| / |𝒫⁺|

𝒫⁺ 为应拒识页面集（图集、列表页等），正常页面集 𝒫⁻ 的误拒率以 𝒫⁻ 为分母另计——两类分母互斥，防止「全部拒识」或「全部接受」抬高单项数字。

03 · The Self-Evolution Loop

自进化环路设计

每一轮迭代都是一次完整的「评估 → 定位 → 发现 → 制定 → 实现 → 版本化 → 回归验证」循环；两个判断节点分别决定「本轮是否保留」与「整个迭代是否终止」。基础设施：loop/run_iteration.py（一键迭代与指标落盘）、loop/layer_timer.py（分层耗时埋点）、loop/calibrate_refusal.py（拒识标定）、loop/probe_*.py（失分探针）。

停滞判据（v15 终止）：v12 +0.013、v13 零（回滚）、v14 +0.044、v15 +0.025；残余失分簇全部落入四类不可继续区——①任务定义差异（17 页拒识口径分歧）②标注口径差异（更新时间 50 页元数据含 dateModified 而不标）③误填风险区（14 页标注为空但页面有可见日期）④段落级正文取舍，属分类头模型适用场景（按任务要求仅设计训练方案、不实际训练，见 §06）。
04 · Metric Curves

指标曲线：逐版本全量重评

每轮迭代对 dev 集（85 个评分页 + 4 个拒识负例，评分器版本冻结）与 ISPRAS 外部基准（160 页 / 80 站）执行全量重评，结果以机器可读形式追加至 loop/metrics_history.jsonl。dev 集在 v8 后趋于饱和（残余失分全部为已登记的口径挂起项），v10 之后的增益全部发生在 ISPRAS——这正是引入外部基准的意义所在。

dev 集指标（85 页 + 4 负例）

v8 封顶；残余失分 = 口径挂起项（cnblogs 标题 3 页、时间字段 7 页、用户名 1 页）；v13 与 v12 聚合持平（其负结果仅体现在 ISPRAS 正文）

ISPRAS 外部基准（160 页英文站）

v13 为实验回退点（正文 0.761→0.752，三角标记，如实呈现回退前指标），随后整体回滚、v14 在回滚后的基线上继续

成本：抽取吞吐对比（页/分，越高越好）

模型补全层按触发门控按需启用——dev 仅 10/89 页、ISPRAS 约 40% 的页面承担约 2 秒/页的模型成本；模型常驻 12GB 统一内存，无 API 调用费用
规则管线主导的改进 模型补全层相关的改进 dev 拒识准确率恒为 1.000，拒识负例自 v9 起 4/4；ISPRAS 更新时间与作者两项存在标注口径差异（悬浮查看口径说明）
05 · Best Plan

最佳方案：v15 规则管线优先 + 门控模型补全

候选终态中，纯规则方案（约 700 页/分、零模型依赖）与全量模型方案（约 30 页/分、且存在编造风险）各据一端；门控方案令模型成本精确落在规则失陷页上——dev 集 11%、ISPRAS 40% 的页面承担全部模型成本，其余页面享受规则速度。生产部署可按吞吐与质量偏好，通过环境变量 EXTRACT_MODEL=1 在两档之间切换。流程各节点悬浮（或键盘聚焦）可查看实现细节。

数据形态流转示例（真实页面逐阶段）

以 ISPRAS 页面 akipress_com__ae4f7a3c（吉尔吉斯斯坦通讯社短讯，触发模型补全层）为例，展示数据在链路各阶段的形态变化（完整输入输出见 §07 样例 2）：

S0原始输入字节流 38,300 B
text/html 字节流：og:title 元标签、<div class="addinfo"> 站点信息行（含 "July 16, 2024 / 11:58 AM"）、正文 <p> 等
S1解码与解析
Unicode 文本 → DOM 树 （声明编码优先；bs4/lxml 解析，script/style/noscript 在可见文本提取时剔除）
S2拒识判定
rejected = false （非列表页 / 图集 / 空壳：链接密度与图说性信号均未达阈值）
S3候选产生
{ title ← meta:og:title ✓；content ← trafilatura 247 字 ✓；authors = 无；publish_time = 无 } （页面元数据无时间、无署名行）
S4规则融合后
title 定值（og:title 无品牌后缀）；publish_time 仍为空 → 命中触发门控
S5模型输入
页面可见文本前 3,500 字符 + 抽取提示词 （提示词全文见上方「模型补全层」节点悬浮框）
S6模型原始输出
{"title": "Check into messages with threats…", "authors": [], "publish_time": "July 16, 2024 / 11:58 AM"}
S7核验与采纳
publish_time：可解析 ✓（英文月名 + "/" 分隔 + AM/PM）· 日期页内佐证 ✓ → 采纳； authors 空数组 → 保持判空；title 已有强来源 → 模型结果不回写
S8精化与终值
publish_time = 2024-07-16 11:58:00 （v15 同日时分精度补全） provenance.publish_time = "model:qwen2.5-7b(verified:parseable | July 16, 2024 / 11:58 AM)" 该页得分：标题 1.00 / 发布时间 1.00 / 作者·更新 正确判空 / 正文 0.69

06 · Training Plans (Design Only)

训练方案设计（仅设计，不实际训练）

路线 A：分类头信息抽取模型优先 · 速度导向

  • 问题定位：规则与大模型都不擅长的「逐块二分类」——①正文段落级取舍（个别页面正文碎为逐段独立元素，容器级选择无解，v13 已证；实例见 §07 样例 4）②署名与时间块的语义确认（区分署名行与分享按钮、推荐位）
  • 数据构造：以本项目 117 页标注与 ISPRAS 160 页为源，按 DOM 块自动银标——块文本与标注正文的 3-gram 重合度高于 0.5 为正例、低于 0.05 为负例，中间带人工复核约 10%（预计 3–5 万块）；按站点族做模板隔离切分；对导航、推荐位、页脚等难负例过采样
  • 模型架构：多语小型编码器（mDeBERTa-v3-base，约 300MB，CPU 可推理）；输入为块文本（截断 256 token）与约 16 维结构特征（标签深度、链接密度、块序位置、样式类名信号等）拼接；输出二分类头，正文 / 署名 / 时间三任务共享编码器多头训练
  • 训练流程：银标预训练 2–3 轮 → 人工复核子集微调 → 按站点族 k 折验证 → 块级 F1 与页级正文 F1 双指标验收（页级不低于现有方案方允许替换）
  • 预期收益：碎正文页面从 0.09 提升至 0.9 以上；ISPRAS 正文预计升至 0.85 以上；推理约 5 毫秒/页（CPU 批推理），较大模型方案快约 400 倍，可全量开启、取代触发门控

路线 B：小型大模型蒸馏备选 · 通用性导向

  • 问题定位：7B 模型零样本已够用，但 2 秒/页与 12GB 常驻内存构成边缘部署瓶颈；且候选裁决类判断（两个候选标题二选一）与标注口径不一致（v14 负结果）——零样本模型不了解本任务的标注口径
  • 数据构造：v10–v15 全部模型调用日志中经核验链通过的正确输出（天然附带「页内可核验」标签，2000 余条）+ 口径挂起项按明确口径文档转为指令样本 + 各轮误填案例构造拒答负样本
  • 模型架构：Qwen2.5-3B + LoRA 微调（秩 16，统一内存可训练），输出保持 JSON 格式约定
  • 训练流程：训练后仍须通过与 v10 相同的输出核验链——核验链是架构的组成部分，不随模型替换而取消
  • 预期收益：补全延迟 2 秒→0.5 秒/页、常驻内存 12GB→3GB；口径对齐后裁决类场景可重新启用（预计标题 +0.02~0.04）
两路线的关系：路线 A 解决「块级取舍」——当前完全无解的场景，属于补盲；路线 B 解决「成本与口径」——大模型已有效但昂贵，属于优化。优先实施路线 A。
07 · Case Gallery

输入输出样例库

六个真实页面案例：输入为完整原始 HTML（面板内滚动查看），输出为 v15 实际产出的完整 JSON 记录。三个满分案例分别覆盖规则链路、模型补全层与拒识判定；三个失分案例对应当前残留的三类不可继续区。字段打分口径见 §02，字段语义见 §01。

news_cn__01 dev 集 · 新华社 · 命中站点规则库，未触发模型补全层（单页约 85ms） 满分案例
输入 · 完整原始 HTML22,092 B

                </div> <div class="head-line clearfix"><h1><span class="title">新华社评出2025年国内十大新闻</span> <span class="btn-audio"></span></h1> <audio id="audioDom" src="" loop="loop" class="hide"></audio> <div class="pageShare"><div class="setFont">字体：
                            <span id="fontSmall">小</span> <span id="fontNormal" class="active">中</span> <span id="fontBig">大</span></div> <div class="share">
                            分享到：<a href="javascript:void(0)" class="wx"></a><a href="javascript:void(0)" class="wb"></a><a href="javascript:void(0)" class="xcx"></a><a href="javascript:void(0)" class="khd"></a> <div class="wx-ewm"><img src="zxcode_20251229d88b731b55844876badbe2a1c7b00476.jpg"></div> <div class="xcx-ewm"><img></div> <div class="khd-ewm"><img src="//www.news.cn/2021detail/images/qrcode-app.png"></div></div></div></div></div></div> <div class="mheader domMobile"><h1><span class="title">新华社评出2025年国内十大新闻</span></h1> <div class="info">
                2025-12-29 08:06:55
                <span>
                    来源：新华网
                </span></div></div> <div class="main clearfix"><div class="main-left"><div id="detail" data="datasource:20251229d88b731b55844876badbe2a1c7b00476" datatype="content"><span id="detailContent"><p>　　新华社北京12月29日电 <span style="color: #000080;"><strong>新华社评出2025年国内十大新闻（按事件发生时间先后为序）</strong></span></p><p><span style="color: #000080;"><strong>　　1.全党扎实开展深入贯彻中央八项规定精神学习教育 推进作风建设常态化长效化</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="zlnRxUReuvv70MOS8W" style="margin: 0px auto; display: block; float: none;" src="R42rCcXRrF6hNwdf.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;2025年6月5日，江苏省南通市崇川区狼山镇街道的党员干部参观以中央八项规定精神为主题的廉政展馆。新华社发（许丛军 摄）</span></p><p>　　自2025年全国两会后，深入贯彻中央八项规定精神学习教育在全党扎实开展，这是习近平总书记亲自谋划的今年党建工作重点任务。广大党员干部深入学习领会习近平总书记关于加强党的作风建设的重要论述，锲而不舍贯彻中央八项规定及其实施细则精神，在一体推进学查改、动真碰硬解决“四风”突出问题和补齐作风建设制度短板、强化制度执行力等方面取得明显成效，推动党的作风实现整体性提升，汇聚起推动经济社会高质量发展的强大力量。</p><p>　<span style="color: #000080;">　<strong>2.中国电影登顶全球动画电影票房榜 中华文化传播力影响力不断提升</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="2JAO2jjOQ2sj7cXzPl" style="margin: 0px auto; display: block; float: none;" src="L6SesOYD28hwoGWE.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;2025年6月25日，在沙特阿拉伯利雅得，观众在《哪吒之魔童闹海》的宣传展板前自拍留念。新华社记者 王海洲 摄</span></p><p>　　3月14日，电影《哪吒之魔童闹海》全球票房超150亿元人民币，位列全球动画电影票房榜首位，影片通过深度挖掘中国故事、彰显中华美学韵味，给人以震撼人心的观影体验，实现了中国电影历史性突破。今年以来，“西夏陵”列入《世界遗产名录》，故宫博物院迎来建院100周年、中外游客络绎不绝，“赫哲族伊玛堪”转入人类非物质文化遗产代表作名录，中式茶饮、中国潮玩等在海外持续“圈粉”，以网络文学、网络游戏、网络影视剧为代表的文化“新三样”加速“出海”，中华文化国际传播力影响力不断提升。</p><p>　<span style="color: #000080;"><strong>　3.重大科技工程取得新突破 我国向高水平科技自立自强加速迈进</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="AlHinhIt975oS2XSBl" style="margin: 0px auto; display: block; float: none;" src="Wuo6yR17qPAXBtTB.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;这是2025年12月9日在北京航天飞行控制中心屏幕上拍摄的神舟二十一号乘组航天员张陆与武飞（右）在舱外工作的画面。新华社记者 刘艺 摄</span></p><p>　　4月以来，神舟二十号、二十一号、二十二号飞船相继飞天，在空间生命科学、空间材料科学、航天新技术等领域持续产出研究成果。5月，天问二号正式开启我国首次小行星探测与采样返回之旅，这是继“探月”“探火”后中国在浩瀚星宇的又一次重要探索。10月，长征系列运载火箭第600次发射在海南文昌告捷，未来将适应更高密度发射需求。以深度求索（DeepSeek）为代表的国产大语言模型推动人工智能技术普遍应用，“奋斗者”号创造北极密集海冰覆盖区进行连续、常规载人深潜新纪录，我国第一艘电磁弹射型航母福建舰入列……一系列科技新突破推动我国向着高水平科技自立自强加速迈进，不断绘就创新中国新图景。</p><p>　<strong><span style="color: #000080;">　4.习近平率中央代表团出席西藏、新疆两个自治区成立庆祝活动 引领推进中华民族共同体建设</span></strong></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="80d5yRViQvpuHWtf11" style="margin: 0px auto; display: block; float: none;" src="FplumoHzrEFkKv1K.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;左图：2025年8月21日上午，彩车上的演员通过西藏拉萨市布达拉宫广场时向人群挥手，热烈庆祝西藏自治区成立60周年。右图：2025年9月23日下午，群众载歌载舞，喜迎新疆维吾尔自治区成立70周年。新华社记者 丁增尼达 毕晓洋 摄</span></p><p>　　习近平作为中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席率中央代表团于8月20日至21日到西藏出席西藏自治区成立60周年庆祝活动、于9月23日至25日到新疆出席新疆维吾尔自治区成立70周年庆祝活动，这在党和国家历史上都是第一次，充分体现了党中央对西藏和新疆工作的高度重视、对各族干部群众的亲切关怀，激励鼓舞各族儿女共同团结奋斗、共同繁荣发展，进一步铸牢中华民族共同体意识、推进中华民族共同体建设，同心携手谱写中国式现代化建设新篇章。</p><p>　　<strong><span style="color: #000080;">5.元首外交引领中国特色大国外交开创新局面 四大全球倡议为世界注入稳定性和正能量</span></strong></p><p><strong><span style="color: #000080;"><img id="vflMbugEaOGDVSI98l" style="display: block; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" src="CDiZLp8mKJIVFPhx.jpg" data-material-id="25122912495712" data-name="202512292f80ce421c2444dd9dc27b3a0f914d26.jpg"></span></strong></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;2025年10月13日上午，国家主席习近平在北京国家会议中心出席全球妇女峰会开幕式并发表主旨讲话。这是习近平和夫人彭丽媛同与会各国和国际组织代表团团长夫妇合影留念。新华社记者 黄敬文 摄</span></p><p>　　8月31日至9月1日，2025年上海合作组织峰会在天津举行。习近平主席在峰会上提出全球治理倡议，这是继全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议之后，中国为推动构建人类命运共同体提出的又一重大全球倡议。2025年，习近平主席出席中央周边工作会议并发表重要讲话，出访越南、马来西亚、柬埔寨等东南亚三国，对俄罗斯进行国事访问并出席纪念苏联伟大卫国战争胜利80周年庆典，赴哈萨克斯坦出席第二届中国-中亚峰会，赴韩国出席亚太经合组织领导人非正式会议并对韩国进行国事访问，举行中美元首会晤，出席全球妇女峰会等主场外交活动，以元首外交引领中国特色大国外交开拓进取、破浪前行。中国理念、中国方案、中国行动为变乱交织的世界持续注入稳定性和正能量。</p><p>　<strong><span style="color: #000080;">　6.隆重纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利80周年 振奋民族精神凝聚奋斗力量</span></strong></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><span style="color: #000080;"><img id="uKIiuPeG5fitUhALza" style="display: block; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" src="rdW1FNktPrqjj48q.jpg" data-material-id="25122900132577" data-name="202512294af0b15dae1a44b487e661e79ae9362c.jpg"></span></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;2025年9月3日，纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利80周年大会在北京天安门广场隆重举行。这是中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席习近平检阅受阅部队。新华社记者 李刚 摄</span></p><p>　　9月3日，纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利80周年大会在北京天安门广场隆重举行，以盛大阅兵仪式，同世界人民一道纪念这个伟大的日子，共同开创更加光明的未来。中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席习近平发表重要讲话并检阅受阅部队。61位外国国家元首、政府首脑及有关国家高级别代表、国际组织负责人、前政要等出席大会。抗战纪念盛典庄严隆重、大气磅礴、震撼人心、激励奋进，进一步弘扬了伟大抗战精神，进一步坚定了全面推进强国建设、民族复兴伟业的信念信心，进一步展示了推动构建人类命运共同体的责任担当。</p><p>　<strong><span style="color: #000080;">　7.党的二十届四中全会胜利召开 擘画未来5年中国发展蓝图</span></strong></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="dQI9RAbpVptgc6efPP" style="display: block; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" src="NvlrFpno5spHRriC.jpg" data-material-id="25122910578188" data-name="20251229614b938d5d24443e9d10d2e11d38ce5e.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;中国共产党第二十届中央委员会第四次全体会议，于2025年10月20日至23日在北京举行。中央政治局主持会议。新华社记者 李响 摄</span></p><p>　　10月20日至23日，党的二十届四中全会在北京召开。全会听取和讨论了习近平总书记受中央政治局委托所作的工作报告，审议通过了《中共中央关于制定国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划的建议》。习近平总书记就《建议》起草的有关情况向全会作了说明。《建议》准确把握“十五五”时期党和国家事业发展所处历史方位，深入分析我国发展环境面临的深刻复杂变化，对未来5年发展作出顶层设计和战略擘画，是乘势而上、接续推进中国式现代化建设的又一次总动员、总部署。全会高度评价“十四五”时期我国发展取得的重大成就。过去5年，以习近平同志为核心的党中央团结带领全党全国各族人民，迎难而上、砥砺前行，有效应对各种冲击挑战，我国经济、科技、国防等硬实力和文化、制度、外交等软实力明显提升，“十四五”即将圆满收官，第二个百年奋斗目标新征程实现良好开局。</p><p>　<strong><span style="color: #000080;">　8.设立台湾光复纪念日 激励两岸同胞为实现祖国完全统一而共同奋斗</span></strong></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="wWMWKaopbWD8kIBNaR" style="margin: 0px auto; display: block; float: none;" src="v1poIGxMe9zP4Q7D.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;2025年10月25日，参观者在中国人民抗日战争纪念馆参观《不屈的宝岛 丹心向祖国——台湾同胞抗日史实展》。新华社记者 张晨霖 摄</span></p><p>　　10月24日，全国人大常委会作出决定，以法律形式将10月25日设立为台湾光复纪念日。党和国家设立台湾光复纪念日，展示了全国各族人民坚持一个中国原则、捍卫国家主权和领土完整的坚定立场，反映了包括台湾同胞在内的海内外中华儿女的共同愿望，彰显了中国共产党坚定不移担当历史任务、矢志不渝实现祖国完全统一的坚强意志，巩固了国际社会坚持世界上只有一个中国、台湾是中国不可分割一部分的普遍共识，必将激励两岸同胞继承和发扬爱国主义传统、伟大抗战精神，为实现祖国完全统一、中华民族伟大复兴而共同奋斗。10月25日，纪念台湾光复80周年大会在京召开。有关部门和地方举办多种形式的纪念活动，各界台胞踊跃参与。11月7日起，针对日本首相高市早苗发表的涉台挑衅言论，中方予以严正交涉和坚决斗争。</p><p><span style="color: #000080;">　　<strong>9.第十五届全运会由粤港澳三地联合举办 成为“一国两制”在体育领域创新实践</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="o67K5E1kK6jNjdS4hn" style="margin: 0px auto; display: block; float: none;" src="3RZnap6Sc9iX19bX.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;2025年11月9日，广东省体育代表团、香港特别行政区体育代表团和澳门特别行政区体育代表团在第十五届全国运动会开幕式上共同入场。新华社记者 赖向东 摄</span></p><p>　　中华人民共和国第十五届运动会于11月9日至21日由广东、香港、澳门三地联合举办。中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席习近平出席开幕式并宣布运动会开幕。本届全运会坚持“绿色、共享、开放、廉洁”的办赛理念和“简约、安全、精彩”的办赛要求，作为“一国两制”在体育领域的创新实践，将办赛工作与推动三地全民健身活动相结合，共同奏响“硬联通”“软联通”“心联通”的乐章，助力粤港澳大湾区高质量发展迈上新台阶。</p><p><strong><span style="color: #000080;">　　10.海南自贸港启动全岛封关 进一步全面深化改革开放推动我国经济顶压前行、向新向优</span></strong></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;"><img id="yozVPTbO1VjfvAP6af" style="margin: 0px auto; display: block; float: none;" src="zxx36dGw11E2Llqe.jpg"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: 楷体; color: #000080;">&emsp;&emsp;2025年12月18日，一艘装载着石化原辅料的外籍船舶泊入位于海南省儋州市的国投洋浦油储码头30万吨级原油泊位（无人机照片）。自2025年12月18日起，海南自由贸易港正式启动全岛封关。新华社记者 郭程 摄</span></p><p>　　12月18日，海南自由贸易港正式启动全岛封关，这是我国坚定不移扩大高水平对外开放、推动建设开放型世界经济的标志性举措。封关后，海南作为海关监管特殊区域，实施以“‘一线’放开、‘二线’管住、岛内自由”为基本特征的政策制度，将成为引领我国新时代对外开放的重要门户。一年来，从施行民营经济促进法、纵深推进全国统一大市场建设，到实施自由贸易试验区提升战略，过境免签政策再扩容、离境退税政策更优化，我国进一步全面深化改革开放迈出新步伐，有力推动我国经济顶压前行、向新向优发展，现代化产业体系建设持续推进，重点领域风险化解取得积极进展，民生保障更加有力。我国经济社会发展主要目标将顺利完成，全年国内生产总值预计达到140万亿元左右。</p></span> <div id="articleEdit"><span class="tiyi1 domPC"><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="advise">【纠错】</a> <div id="advisebox01" class="tiyi01" style="display:none;"><div><iframe id="jc_link1" border="0" marginwidth="0" framespacing="0" marginheight="0" frameborder="0" noresize="noresize" scrolling="no" vspale="0" style="width:600px;height:350px;float:left;"></iframe></div> <div class="tiyi03"><div id="jc_close1" style="cursor:pointer;"></div></div></div></span> <span class="editor"> 【责任编辑:王萌萌】 </span></div></div> <div class="columBox relatedNews" data="datasource:20251229d88b731b55844876badbe2a1c7b00476" datatype="content"> <div class="col-cont"><ul></ul></div></div> <div class="nextpage clearfix" style="display:none"><div class="nextpage-tit">阅读下一篇：</div> <div class="nextpage-cont"><a href="###"></a></div></div></div></div> <div class="foot"><script src="//lib.xinhuanet.com/common/foot.js"></script></div> <div data="datasource:20251229d88b731b55844876badbe2a1c7b00476" datatype="content"><div id="fontsize" style="display:none;">

  "content_text": "新华社北京12月29日电 新华社评出2025年国内十大新闻（按事件发生时间先后为序）\n1.全党扎实开展深入贯彻中央八项规定精神学习教育 推进作风建设常态化长效化\n[[IMG_1]]\n自2025年全国两会后，深入贯彻中央八项规定精神学习教育在全党扎实开展，这是习近平总书记亲自谋划的今年党建工作重点任务。广大党员干部深入学习领会习近平总书记关于加强党的作风建设的重要论述，锲而不舍贯彻中央八项规定及其实施细则精神，在一体推进学查改、动真碰硬解决“四风”突出问题和补齐作风建设制度短板、强化制度执行力等方面取得明显成效，推动党的作风实现整体性提升，汇聚起推动经济社会高质量发展的强大力量。\n2.中国电影登顶全球动画电影票房榜 中华文化传播力影响力不断提升\n[[IMG_2]]\n3月14日，电影《哪吒之魔童闹海》全球票房超150亿元人民币，位列全球动画电影票房榜首位，影片通过深度挖掘中国故事、彰显中华美学韵味，给人以震撼人心的观影体验，实现了中国电影历史性突破。今年以来，“西夏陵”列入《世界遗产名录》，故宫博物院迎来建院100周年、中外游客络绎不绝，“赫哲族伊玛堪”转入人类非物质文化遗产代表作名录，中式茶饮、中国潮玩等在海外持续“圈粉”，以网络文学、网络游戏、网络影视剧为代表的文化“新三样”加速“出海”，中华文化国际传播力影响力不断提升。\n3.重大科技工程取得新突破 我国向高水平科技自立自强加速迈进\n[[IMG_3]]\n4月以来，神舟二十号、二十一号、二十二号飞船相继飞天，在空间生命科学、空间材料科学、航天新技术等领域持续产出研究成果。5月，天问二号正式开启我国首次小行星探测与采样返回之旅，这是继“探月”“探火”后中国在浩瀚星宇的又一次重要探索。10月，长征系列运载火箭第600次发射在海南文昌告捷，未来将适应更高密度发射需求。以深度求索（DeepSeek）为代表的国产大语言模型推动人工智能技术普遍应用，“奋斗者”号创造北极密集海冰覆盖区进行连续、常规载人深潜新纪录，我国第一艘电磁弹射型航母福建舰入列……一系列科技新突破推动我国向着高水平科技自立自强加速迈进，不断绘就创新中国新图景。\n4.习近平率中央代表团出席西藏、新疆两个自治区成立庆祝活动 引领推进中华民族共同体建设\n[[IMG_4]]\n习近平作为中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席率中央代表团于8月20日至21日到西藏出席西藏自治区成立60周年庆祝活动、于9月23日至25日到新疆出席新疆维吾尔自治区成立70周年庆祝活动，这在党和国家历史上都是第一次，充分体现了党中央对西藏和新疆工作的高度重视、对各族干部群众的亲切关怀，激励鼓舞各族儿女共同团结奋斗、共同繁荣发展，进一步铸牢中华民族共同体意识、推进中华民族共同体建设，同心携手谱写中国式现代化建设新篇章。\n5.元首外交引领中国特色大国外交开创新局面 四大全球倡议为世界注入稳定性和正能量\n[[IMG_5]]\n8月31日至9月1日，2025年上海合作组织峰会在天津举行。习近平主席在峰会上提出全球治理倡议，这是继全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议之后，中国为推动构建人类命运共同体提出的又一重大全球倡议。2025年，习近平主席出席中央周边工作会议并发表重要讲话，出访越南、马来西亚、柬埔寨等东南亚三国，对俄罗斯进行国事访问并出席纪念苏联伟大卫国战争胜利80周年庆典，赴哈萨克斯坦出席第二届中国-中亚峰会，赴韩国出席亚太经合组织领导人非正式会议并对韩国进行国事访问，举行中美元首会晤，出席全球妇女峰会等主场外交活动，以元首外交引领中国特色大国外交开拓进取、破浪前行。中国理念、中国方案、中国行动为变乱交织的世界持续注入稳定性和正能量。\n6.隆重纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利80周年 振奋民族精神凝聚奋斗力量\n[[IMG_6]]\n9月3日，纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利80周年大会在北京天安门广场隆重举行，以盛大阅兵仪式，同世界人民一道纪念这个伟大的日子，共同开创更加光明的未来。中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席习近平发表重要讲话并检阅受阅部队。61位外国国家元首、政府首脑及有关国家高级别代表、国际组织负责人、前政要等出席大会。抗战纪念盛典庄严隆重、大气磅礴、震撼人心、激励奋进，进一步弘扬了伟大抗战精神，进一步坚定了全面推进强国建设、民族复兴伟业的信念信心，进一步展示了推动构建人类命运共同体的责任担当。\n7.党的二十届四中全会胜利召开 擘画未来5年中国发展蓝图\n[[IMG_7]]\n10月20日至23日，党的二十届四中全会在北京召开。全会听取和讨论了习近平总书记受中央政治局委托所作的工作报告，审议通过了《中共中央关于制定国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划的建议》。习近平总书记就《建议》起草的有关情况向全会作了说明。《建议》准确把握“十五五”时期党和国家事业发展所处历史方位，深入分析我国发展环境面临的深刻复杂变化，对未来5年发展作出顶层设计和战略擘画，是乘势而上、接续推进中国式现代化建设的又一次总动员、总部署。全会高度评价“十四五”时期我国发展取得的重大成就。过去5年，以习近平同志为核心的党中央团结带领全党全国各族人民，迎难而上、砥砺前行，有效应对各种冲击挑战，我国经济、科技、国防等硬实力和文化、制度、外交等软实力明显提升，“十四五”即将圆满收官，第二个百年奋斗目标新征程实现良好开局。\n8.设立台湾光复纪念日 激励两岸同胞为实现祖国完全统一而共同奋斗\n[[IMG_8]]\n10月24日，全国人大常委会作出决定，以法律形式将10月25日设立为台湾光复纪念日。党和国家设立台湾光复纪念日，展示了全国各族人民坚持一个中国原则、捍卫国家主权和领土完整的坚定立场，反映了包括台湾同胞在内的海内外中华儿女的共同愿望，彰显了中国共产党坚定不移担当历史任务、矢志不渝实现祖国完全统一的坚强意志，巩固了国际社会坚持世界上只有一个中国、台湾是中国不可分割一部分的普遍共识，必将激励两岸同胞继承和发扬爱国主义传统、伟大抗战精神，为实现祖国完全统一、中华民族伟大复兴而共同奋斗。10月25日，纪念台湾光复80周年大会在京召开。有关部门和地方举办多种形式的纪念活动，各界台胞踊跃参与。11月7日起，针对日本首相高市早苗发表的涉台挑衅言论，中方予以严正交涉和坚决斗争。\n9.第十五届全运会由粤港澳三地联合举办 成为“一国两制”在体育领域创新实践\n[[IMG_9]]\n中华人民共和国第十五届运动会于11月9日至21日由广东、香港、澳门三地联合举办。中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席习近平出席开幕式并宣布运动会开幕。本届全运会坚持“绿色、共享、开放、廉洁”的办赛理念和“简约、安全、精彩”的办赛要求，作为“一国两制”在体育领域的创新实践，将办赛工作与推动三地全民健身活动相结合，共同奏响“硬联通”“软联通”“心联通”的乐章，助力粤港澳大湾区高质量发展迈上新台阶。\n10.海南自贸港启动全岛封关 进一步全面深化改革开放推动我国经济顶压前行、向新向优\n[[IMG_10]]\n12月18日，海南自由贸易港正式启动全岛封关，这是我国坚定不移扩大高水平对外开放、推动建设开放型世界经济的标志性举措。封关后，海南作为海关监管特殊区域，实施以“‘一线’放开、‘二线’管住、岛内自由”为基本特征的政策制度，将成为引领我国新时代对外开放的重要门户。一年来，从施行民营经济促进法、纵深推进全国统一大市场建设，到实施自由贸易试验区提升战略，过境免签政策再扩容、离境退税政策更优化，我国进一步全面深化改革开放迈出新步伐，有力推动我国经济顶压前行、向新向优发展，现代化产业体系建设持续推进，重点领域风险化解取得积极进展，民生保障更加有力。我国经济社会发展主要目标将顺利完成，全年国内生产总值预计达到140万亿元左右。\n【纠错】             <div id="ContentTab" class="content active">
    <div class="widget widget-ArticleFulltext widget-instance-OUP_Article_FullText_Widget">
        <div class="module-widget">
    <div class="widget-items" data-widgetname="ArticleFulltext"><div class="article-metadata-standalone-panel clearfix" style="display: block;"><div class="article-metadata-tocSections">
                    <div class="article-metadata-tocSections-title">Issue Section:</div>
                        <a href="/ejil/search-results?f_TocHeadingTitleList=Book+Reviews" data-google-interstitial="false">Book Reviews</a>
                </div></div>





<p class="chapter-para">It is difficult to condense the contents of Freya Baetens’ edited collection <em>Identity and Diversity on the International Bench</em>, with its 26 chapters, divided into three parts (‘Towards the International Bench’, ‘On the International Bench’ and ‘Beyond the International Bench’), with a brief but engaging foreword by Navanethem Pillay and an epilogue entrusted to Janet Nosworthy. The book includes many insightful references to the personal experiences of these and other contributors – both before attaining the international bench and during their terms in office. However, its main interest lies in offering a ‘holistic’ approach to the issue of diversity within international courts and tribunals. In this respect, the editor’s stated aim to ‘provide a more comprehensive and in-depth look at the impact of identity on (the legitimacy of) international adjudication’ (Baetens, at 5) is certainly achieved. At the same time, the ‘holistic’ approach leads to frequent overlaps between chapters, and the distinction between the three parts of the book is not always fully reflected in the contribution’s contents. Moreover, some additional guidance on the links and connections between the different chapters might have helped the reader navigate the wealth of material included in this complex book.</p><p class="chapter-para">That said, the volume is a welcome addition to the literature discussing diversity in international arbitration and adjudication. There is little doubt that the legitimacy of the composition of a court (be it international or domestic) is a key element of procedural fairness, in the view both of the parties and of that court’s constituencies more generally. The book is based on the idea that diversity is key to international courts’ normative and social legitimacy, not only at the domestic level (where it is deemed a component of democracy) but also in regard to international courts. However, this is not taken for granted: both Baetens' introductory chapter and several contributions critically discuss this point – rightly so, as how a diverse composition of the bench and the identity of judges can influence the legitimacy of a court is highly contextual, and legitimacy as such has a ‘supremely intangible quality’ (Nosworthy, at 544). Also, in light of this, the experiences of very different courts and tribunals are not always easy to compare, but the identity-diversity conundrum affects them all. Thus, looking at how the challenge is tackled in one area may help to put in focus analogous challenges and possible solutions in a different context.</p><p class="chapter-para"><em>Identity and Diversity on the International Bench</em> attempts this by analysing the relevance of adjudicators’ identity in different jurisdictional scenarios, ranging from interstate courts such as the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) to the World Trade Organization’s (WTO) dispute settlement system, international and internationalized criminal courts and international human rights courts, while also covering commercial and investment arbitration. There are, moreover, some interesting incursions into domestic jurisdictions – for instance, in Clara María López Rodríguez’s chapter on the establishment of indigenous jurisdiction in Peru. While discussing the problems of such jurisdiction, she argues that it might inspire ways of ‘enabl[ing] participation of indigenous peoples in international decision-making’ (at 500) in ways that could protect indigenous rights and that may be preferable to the inclusion on the bench of judges self-identifying as members of indigenous communities, which would require their assimilation (at 501–502). With respect to a different aspect of identity, Kristen Hessler discusses how the US Supreme Court’s composition affected its case law on reproductive rights when addressing the significance of religious diversity in international human rights adjudication.</p><p class="chapter-para">The possibility of meaningful comparisons is perhaps most obvious for gender diversity within the international bench, which is the book’s main focus. It is reflected, for instance, in the discussion (in various chapters, including Baetens’ introduction) of what amounts to adequate gender representation within the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) and whether the ECtHR’s approach might be transferred to other jurisdictions. Several other contributions deal with the (lack of) gender diversity on the international bench. These chapters offer insightful statistics, discuss the rules and practices concerning appointments to different international courts and tribunals, analyse the particular hurdles that women face in this process and speculate on how they might best be overcome. In this respect, the book illustrates the uneven state of play: in international criminal law, women judges have contributed to the development of specific strands of case law (as acknowledged and explored notably by Teresa Doherty in her analysis of the case law related to sexual violence and by Juan-Pablo Pérez-León-Acevedo in his chapters on victims’ status respectively at the International Criminal Court (ICC), the Special Tribunal for Lebanon and the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia).</p><p class="chapter-para">Elsewhere, though, the position is more ambiguous. With respect to the WTO’s dispute settlement system, Valerie Hughes argues that ‘[p]erhaps not all trade disputes will require or benefit from a feminist perspective, but … it is reasonable to suspect that some could’ (at 354), while James Crawford, reflecting on his experience at the ICJ and in international arbitration, ‘could not come up with any defining features which characterizes [female adjudicators’] style, that could be linked to the fact that they are women’ (at 417). Nevertheless, diversity, including gender diversity, is usually beneficial to the adjudication process. As several contributors point out, diversity should never come at the cost of lowering professional standards (see Jamal Seifi, at 165); at the same time, diversity increases not only courts’ legitimacy but also their collective ability to fully appreciate the different implications of a case (see, for example, Baetens, at 8ff; David Bigge, at 64; Nosworthy, at 541, 545), ultimately facilitating access to justice for under-represented groups (Rebecca Emiene Badejogbin, at 127, with reference to women and children).</p><p class="chapter-para">Gender diversity may also fulfil applicable legal standards, which are at times included in the constitutive instruments of international tribunals. This is the case for Article 36(8)(a)(iii) of the ICC’s Rome Statute, which stresses the need to ensure a ‘fair representation of female and male judges’ and is one of the most advanced provisions in this respect.<span class="xrefLink" id="jumplink-fn0001"></span><a href="javascript:;" reveal-id="fn0001" data-open="fn0001" class="link link-ref link-reveal xref-fn js-xref-fn" data-google-interstitial="false"><sup>1</sup></a> In other cases, standards are developed within the institutional context to which a court belongs. Notable examples are the minimum voting requirements adopted by the Assembly of States Parties to the ICC, discussed by Solomy Balungi Bossa and Gilles Landry Dossan in their chapter devoted to ‘Ethnicity, Religion, and Diversity at the International Criminal Court’, and the resolutions of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe concerning the composition of the ECtHR, addressed by Helen Keller, Corina Heri and Myriam Christ in the chapter on ‘Fifty Years of Women at the European Court of Human Rights’. The potential relevance of provisions such as Article 8 of the UN Charter and Article 8 of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women for the composition of international courts is discussed by Liesbeth Lijnzaad in ‘The Smurfette Principle’, which explores the appointment processes for ICJ, ITLOS and ICC judges and the difficulties of broadening the ‘pool’ of qualified female candidates for an international bench in the first place and of ensuring equal chances of success.<span class="xrefLink" id="jumplink-fn0002"></span><a href="javascript:;" reveal-id="fn0002" data-open="fn0002" class="link link-ref link-reveal xref-fn js-xref-fn" data-google-interstitial="false"><sup>2</sup></a> As Lijnzaad shows, these hurdles not only concern the ability of candidates to successfully navigate the path towards appointment – which has a very political component, notably for interstate courts.</p><p class="chapter-para">They are also relevant as candidates aim to obtain the qualifications and experiences necessary to be seriously considered for the position in the first place, starting from adequate education. This point is made also by Rolf Einar Fife in his chapter on incentives devised to induce gender-balanced appointments and by Rebecca Emiene Badejogbin in her discussion of success stories of African female judges. Catherine Drummond delves into the issue of ad hoc arbitration, with an interesting and insightful reflection on the difficulties facing female candidates to be seriously considered for appointment, notwithstanding pledges and campaigns to increase the number of female arbitrators. Drummond’s chapter highlights the reluctance of disputing parties to depart from what are perceived as ‘safe’ and predictable choices, which is also present in interstate litigation. Drummond’s caution against implicit bias and her suggestion that ‘practitioners involved in the selection and appointment process should make a conscious effort to afford female candidates an equal opportunity’ (at 120) has resonance well beyond the context of ad hoc arbitration. Indeed, such ‘conscious efforts’ are necessary to achieve an appropriate gender balance and to avoid retrogressive steps, as experienced, for instance, with respect to ECtHR appointments (Baetens, at 16; Keller, Heri and Christ, at 185). The efforts of the African Union to achieve gender balance in the African Court of Human and Peoples’ Rights, discussed by J. Jarpa Dawuni, show that progress can indeed be made.</p><p class="chapter-para">While gender remains central, the contributors (themselves a very diverse group) also address multiple other factors contributing to an adjudicator’s identity – including, but not limited to, nationality, ethnicity, religion, culture and professional backgrounds – as well as the relevance of those factors in the context of different jurisdictions. Paolo Palchetti’s thought-provoking assessment of the different functions of ICJ judges ad hoc and their role in ensuring diversity on the bench exemplifies the richness of the reflections offered in this book. Palchetti notes the recent trend towards appointing judges ad hoc who are not nationals of the appointing state nor belong to the same geographical group, which is usually seen as a positive development since it enhances the ad hoc judges’ perceived impartiality and ‘public relations’ function. At the same time, he cautions that such judges ad hoc are mostly nationals of the ‘Western and others’ group, which affects the geographical diversity of the bench and the ‘representational’ function, which, as Palchetti stresses, remains a prominent aspect of the judge’s ad hoc role.</p><p class="chapter-para">Seifi’s analysis of diversity and legitimacy in investor-state arbitration also implicitly focuses on the representation function of arbitrators: he draws attention to the different ‘waves’ of (North-South and North-North) investor-state cases and convincingly argues that enhancing gender diversity would not be enough to overcome the development bias in this context; rather, ‘it is imperative to move beyond symbolic steps merely focusing on one diversity indicator’ (167). Another personal highlight is Stacie Strong’s argument in favour of judicial education for international judges, especially those who have no previous experience of adjudication at the domestic level. Not all her suggestions are fully convincing: as the author herself recognizes, a (possibly mandatory) judicial education system for the international bench might meet with significant opposition. Moreover, while international judges with experience on domestic benches may well possess abilities such as ‘court craft’, ‘judicial craft’ and ‘profession craft’ (see Strong’s remarks at 233), they could lack in-depth knowledge of the substantive (international) law they are called upon to apply – a shortcoming that arguably would be more serious and more difficult to overcome than the lack of ‘soft skills’ that can be gained through judicial education. Some of those skills (notably, the ability to interact with fellow judges in a collaborative way or to write in a clear style appropriate to judicial pronouncements) are at least in part innate or, at any rate, more difficult to develop at an advanced career stage. In any case, Strong is right to stress that these qualities are relevant to judicial selection processes in the first place and that they cannot be taken for granted among those called to the international bench. The question as to whether other, less formalized mechanisms for transmitting these skills – such as collegial methods of work or the assistance and institutional memory entrusted to registries (compare with Angelica Nußberger and Freya Baetens, ‘Diversity on the Bench of the European Court of Human Rights: A Clash of Paradigms’) – may be sufficient for this purpose does not find an easy or necessarily uniform answer.</p><p class="chapter-para">The chapter by Nußberger and Baetens also deserves a mention for the nuanced and yet illuminating way in which the authors discuss the role of factors such as age and political affiliation – alongside judges’ legal, cultural and professional backgrounds, which are also in focus in other contributions – in shaping a court’s identity. Several authors, moreover, address the peculiar role of religion in the diversity debate. In his chapter, Bigge notably contends that religious diversity, as opposed to cultural diversity, is not as such an added value in the composition of an international bench – especially as ‘there are few instances in international adjudication in which it would be appropriate to apply religious “culture” to a dispute’ (at 69) – and questions the legitimacy of recourse to religious arguments in judicial or arbitral pronouncements. Mubarak Waseem’s survey of individual opinions by ICJ judges, on the other hand, shows a pattern of references to religious traditions, which are usually not the ones to which these judges belong. In his view, these references are ‘a route by which judges can acknowledge the long-term contributions of other societies to international law’ (Waseem, at 276) and could allow ‘the Court to extend both the geographical and temporal support it can call upon to reinforce basic norms of international law’ (at 278).</p><p class="chapter-para">These accounts of select chapters highlight the richness of the collection edited by Freya Baetens. The numerous contributions and the wide variety of topics they address, without a close dialogue or cross-references between the different authors, make it difficult to draw a set of coherent conclusions. That said, as will be clear from the preceding summary, the book does put forward many thought-provoking arguments in favour of enhancing diversity on the international bench; the wealth of input it offers will help readers confirm – or reconsider – their own views on the diversity and legitimacy of international courts and tribunals, on international justice and, ultimately, on the ‘legitimacy of international law itself’ (Nosworthy, at 539).</p>                    <h2 scrollto-destination="447195985" id="447195985" class="backfootnotegroup-title js-splitscreen-backfootnotegroup-title">Footnotes</h2>
<div content-id="fn0001" class="footnote"><span class="fn"><span class="label fn-label"><span rel="nofollow" data-fn-id="fn0001" class="end-note-link">1</span></span><div class="footnote-content"><p class="footnote-compatibility">Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court 1998, 2187 UNTS 90.</p></div></span></div><div content-id="fn0002" class="footnote"><span class="fn"><span class="label fn-label"><span rel="nofollow" data-fn-id="fn0002" class="end-note-link">2</span></span><div class="footnote-content"><p class="footnote-compatibility">Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women 1979, 1249 UNTS 13.</p></div></span></div>    <!-- /foreach in Model.Sections -->

{
  "id": "ispras__oup_com__427c9d0e",

  "title": "Serena Forlati, Review of Freya Baetens (ed.), Identity and Diversity on the International Bench: Who Is the Judge?",
  "authors": [
    "Forlati",
    "Serena"
  ],
  "publish_time": {
    "value": "2024-03-11 XX:XX:XX",

  "update_time": null,
  "content_text": "[[IMG_1]]\nPDF\nSplit View\nViews\nCiteCiteSerena Forlati, Serena Forlati, Review of Freya Baetens (ed.), Identity and Diversity on the International Bench: Who Is the Judge?, European Journal of International Law, Volume 35, Issue 1, February 2024, Pages 247–251, https://doi.org/10.1093/ejil/chae010Close\nShare Icon Share\nIt is difficult to condense the contents of Freya Baetens’ edited collection Identity and Diversity on the International Bench, with its 26 chapters, divided into three parts (‘Towards the International Bench’, ‘On the International Bench’ and ‘Beyond the International Bench’), with a brief but engaging foreword by Navanethem Pillay and an epilogue entrusted to Janet Nosworthy. The book includes many insightful references to the personal experiences of these and other contributors – both before attaining the international bench and during their terms in office. However, its main interest lies in offering a ‘holistic’ approach to the issue of diversity within international courts and tribunals. In this respect, the editor’s stated aim to ‘provide a more comprehensive and in-depth look at the impact of identity on (the legitimacy of) international adjudication’ (Baetens, at 5) is certainly achieved. At the same time, the ‘holistic’ approach leads to frequent overlaps between chapters, and the distinction between the three parts of the book is not always fully reflected in the contribution’s contents. Moreover, some additional guidance on the links and connections between the different chapters might have helped the reader navigate the wealth of material included in this complex book.\nThat said, the volume is a welcome addition to the literature discussing diversity in international arbitration and adjudication. There is little doubt that the legitimacy of the composition of a court (be it international or domestic) is a key element of procedural fairness, in the view both of the parties and of that court’s constituencies more generally. The book is based on the idea that diversity is key to international courts’ normative and social legitimacy, not only at the domestic level (where it is deemed a component of democracy) but also in regard to international courts. However, this is not taken for granted: both Baetens' introductory chapter and several contributions critically discuss this point – rightly so, as how a diverse composition of the bench and the identity of judges can influence the legitimacy of a court is highly contextual, and legitimacy as such has a ‘supremely intangible quality’ (Nosworthy, at 544). Also, in light of this, the experiences of very different courts and tribunals are not always easy to compare, but the identity-diversity conundrum affects them all. Thus, looking at how the challenge is tackled in one area may help to put in focus analogous challenges and possible solutions in a different context.\nIdentity and Diversity on the International Bench attempts this by analysing the relevance of adjudicators’ identity in different jurisdictional scenarios, ranging from interstate courts such as the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) to the World Trade Organization’s (WTO) dispute settlement system, international and internationalized criminal courts and international human rights courts, while also covering commercial and investment arbitration. There are, moreover, some interesting incursions into domestic jurisdictions – for instance, in Clara María López Rodríguez’s chapter on the establishment of indigenous jurisdiction in Peru. While discussing the problems of such jurisdiction, she argues that it might inspire ways of ‘enabl[ing] participation of indigenous peoples in international decision-making’ (at 500) in ways that could protect indigenous rights and that may be preferable to the inclusion on the bench of judges self-identifying as members of indigenous communities, which would require their assimilation (at 501–502). With respect to a different aspect of identity, Kristen Hessler discusses how the US Supreme Court’s composition affected its case law on reproductive rights when addressing the significance of religious diversity in international human rights adjudication.\nThe possibility of meaningful comparisons is perhaps most obvious for gender diversity within the international bench, which is the book’s main focus. It is reflected, for instance, in the discussion (in various chapters, including Baetens’ introduction) of what amounts to adequate gender representation within the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) and whether the ECtHR’s approach might be transferred to other jurisdictions. Several other contributions deal with the (lack of) gender diversity on the international bench. These chapters offer insightful statistics, discuss the rules and practices concerning appointments to different international courts and tribunals, analyse the particular hurdles that women face in this process and speculate on how they might best be overcome. In this respect, the book illustrates the uneven state of play: in international criminal law, women judges have contributed to the development of specific strands of case law (as acknowledged and explored notably by Teresa Doherty in her analysis of the case law related to sexual violence and by Juan-Pablo Pérez-León-Acevedo in his chapters on victims’ status respectively at the International Criminal Court (ICC), the Special Tribunal for Lebanon and the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia).\nElsewhere, though, the position is more ambiguous. With respect to the WTO’s dispute settlement system, Valerie Hughes argues that ‘[p]erhaps not all trade disputes will require or benefit from a feminist perspective, but … it is reasonable to suspect that some could’ (at 354), while James Crawford, reflecting on his experience at the ICJ and in international arbitration, ‘could not come up with any defining features which characterizes [female adjudicators’] style, that could be linked to the fact that they are women’ (at 417). Nevertheless, diversity, including gender diversity, is usually beneficial to the adjudication process. As several contributors point out, diversity should never come at the cost of lowering professional standards (see Jamal Seifi, at 165); at the same time, diversity increases not only courts’ legitimacy but also their collective ability to fully appreciate the different implications of a case (see, for example, Baetens, at 8ff; David Bigge, at 64; Nosworthy, at 541, 545), ultimately facilitating access to justice for under-represented groups (Rebecca Emiene Badejogbin, at 127, with reference to women and children).\nGender diversity may also fulfil applicable legal standards, which are at times included in the constitutive instruments of international tribunals. This is the case for Article 36(8)(a)(iii) of the ICC’s Rome Statute, which stresses the need to ensure a ‘fair representation of female and male judges’ and is one of the most advanced provisions in this respect.1 In other cases, standards are developed within the institutional context to which a court belongs. Notable examples are the minimum voting requirements adopted by the Assembly of States Parties to the ICC, discussed by Solomy Balungi Bossa and Gilles Landry Dossan in their chapter devoted to ‘Ethnicity, Religion, and Diversity at the International Criminal Court’, and the resolutions of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe concerning the composition of the ECtHR, addressed by Helen Keller, Corina Heri and Myriam Christ in the chapter on ‘Fifty Years of Women at the European Court of Human Rights’. The potential relevance of provisions such as Article 8 of the UN Charter and Article 8 of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women for the composition of international courts is discussed by Liesbeth Lijnzaad in ‘The Smurfette Principle’, which explores the appointment processes for ICJ, ITLOS and ICC judges and the difficulties of broadening the ‘pool’ of qualified female candidates for an international bench in the first place and of ensuring equal chances of success.2 As Lijnzaad shows, these hurdles not only concern the ability of candidates to successfully navigate the path towards appointment – which has a very political component, notably for interstate courts.\nThey are also relevant as candidates aim to obtain the qualifications and experiences necessary to be seriously considered for the position in the first place, starting from adequate education. This point is made also by Rolf Einar Fife in his chapter on incentives devised to induce gender-balanced appointments and by Rebecca Emiene Badejogbin in her discussion of success stories of African female judges. Catherine Drummond delves into the issue of ad hoc arbitration, with an interesting and insightful reflection on the difficulties facing female candidates to be seriously considered for appointment, notwithstanding pledges and campaigns to increase the number of female arbitrators. Drummond’s chapter highlights the reluctance of disputing parties to depart from what are perceived as ‘safe’ and predictable choices, which is also present in interstate litigation. Drummond’s caution against implicit bias and her suggestion that ‘practitioners involved in the selection and appointment process should make a conscious effort to afford female candidates an equal opportunity’ (at 120) has resonance well beyond the context of ad hoc arbitration. Indeed, such ‘conscious efforts’ are necessary to achieve an appropriate gender balance and to avoid retrogressive steps, as experienced, for instance, with respect to ECtHR appointments (Baetens, at 16; Keller, Heri and Christ, at 185). The efforts of the African Union to achieve gender balance in the African Court of Human and Peoples’ Rights, discussed by J. Jarpa Dawuni, show that progress can indeed be made.\nWhile gender remains central, the contributors (themselves a very diverse group) also address multiple other factors contributing to an adjudicator’s identity – including, but not limited to, nationality, ethnicity, religion, culture and professional backgrounds – as well as the relevance of those factors in the context of different jurisdictions. Paolo Palchetti’s thought-provoking assessment of the different functions of ICJ judges ad hoc and their role in ensuring diversity on the bench exemplifies the richness of the reflections offered in this book. Palchetti notes the recent trend towards appointing judges ad hoc who are not nationals of the appointing state nor belong to the same geographical group, which is usually seen as a positive development since it enhances the ad hoc judges’ perceived impartiality and ‘public relations’ function. At the same time, he cautions that such judges ad hoc are mostly nationals of the ‘Western and others’ group, which affects the geographical diversity of the bench and the ‘representational’ function, which, as Palchetti stresses, remains a prominent aspect of the judge’s ad hoc role.\nSeifi’s analysis of diversity and legitimacy in investor-state arbitration also implicitly focuses on the representation function of arbitrators: he draws attention to the different ‘waves’ of (North-South and North-North) investor-state cases and convincingly argues that enhancing gender diversity would not be enough to overcome the development bias in this context; rather, ‘it is imperative to move beyond symbolic steps merely focusing on one diversity indicator’ (167). Another personal highlight is Stacie Strong’s argument in favour of judicial education for international judges, especially those who have no previous experience of adjudication at the domestic level. Not all her suggestions are fully convincing: as the author herself recognizes, a (possibly mandatory) judicial education system for the international bench might meet with significant opposition. Moreover, while international judges with experience on domestic benches may well possess abilities such as ‘court craft’, ‘judicial craft’ and ‘profession craft’ (see Strong’s remarks at 233), they could lack in-depth knowledge of the substantive (international) law they are called upon to apply – a shortcoming that arguably would be more serious and more difficult to overcome than the lack of ‘soft skills’ that can be gained through judicial education. Some of those skills (notably, the ability to interact with fellow judges in a collaborative way or to write in a clear style appropriate to judicial pronouncements) are at least in part innate or, at any rate, more difficult to develop at an advanced career stage. In any case, Strong is right to stress that these qualities are relevant to judicial selection processes in the first place and that they cannot be taken for granted among those called to the international bench. The question as to whether other, less formalized mechanisms for transmitting these skills – such as collegial methods of work or the assistance and institutional memory entrusted to registries (compare with Angelica Nußberger and Freya Baetens, ‘Diversity on the Bench of the European Court of Human Rights: A Clash of Paradigms’) – may be sufficient for this purpose does not find an easy or necessarily uniform answer.\nThe chapter by Nußberger and Baetens also deserves a mention for the nuanced and yet illuminating way in which the authors discuss the role of factors such as age and political affiliation – alongside judges’ legal, cultural and professional backgrounds, which are also in focus in other contributions – in shaping a court’s identity. Several authors, moreover, address the peculiar role of religion in the diversity debate. In his chapter, Bigge notably contends that religious diversity, as opposed to cultural diversity, is not as such an added value in the composition of an international bench – especially as ‘there are few instances in international adjudication in which it would be appropriate to apply religious “culture” to a dispute’ (at 69) – and questions the legitimacy of recourse to religious arguments in judicial or arbitral pronouncements. Mubarak Waseem’s survey of individual opinions by ICJ judges, on the other hand, shows a pattern of references to religious traditions, which are usually not the ones to which these judges belong. In his view, these references are ‘a route by which judges can acknowledge the long-term contributions of other societies to international law’ (Waseem, at 276) and could allow ‘the Court to extend both the geographical and temporal support it can call upon to reinforce basic norms of international law’ (at 278).\nThese accounts of select chapters highlight the richness of the collection edited by Freya Baetens. The numerous contributions and the wide variety of topics they address, without a close dialogue or cross-references between the different authors, make it difficult to draw a set of coherent conclusions. That said, as will be clear from the preceding summary, the book does put forward many thought-provoking arguments in favour of enhancing diversity on the international bench; the wealth of input it offers will help readers confirm – or reconsider – their own views on the diversity and legitimacy of international courts and tribunals, on international justice and, ultimately, on the ‘legitimacy of international law itself’ (Nosworthy, at 539).\nFootnotes\nRome Statute of the International Criminal Court 1998, 2187 UNTS 90.\nConvention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women 1979, 1249 UNTS 13.",

          </div><!-- /.c-page-hero__meta -->

        <h1 class="c-page-hero__title [ u-fs36 u-fs50@l u-lh1 u-wbbw ]" dir="ltr" lang="en">
      Coups, Conflicts, and a New Era in Africa
    </h1><!-- /.c-page-hero__title -->

    
          <div class="c-page-hero__teaser [ u-ptserif u-fs18 u-fs15@m u-fs18@l u-fsi ]" dir="ltr" lang="en">
        <div class="word-wrap" style="font-weight: 400;"><p style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">This week on <a href="https://www.crisisgroup.org/africa/horn-africa/horn" target="_blank" style="font-weight: 400;">The Horn</a>, Alan hosts a roundtable discussion with Dr Solomon Ayele Dersso, Paul-Simon Handy, and Crisis Group’s Liesl Louw-Vaudran to discuss the state of African peace and security and the African Union’s response to conflicts and crises on the continent. </span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
</div>
      </div><!-- /.c-page-hero__teaser -->
      </div><!-- /.c-page-hero__details -->

</div><!-- /.c-page-hero -->

      <div class="s-article__main s-copy u-display-flex u-flexdc u-flexdr@m u-flexww@m" dir="ltr" lang="en">
        <div class="s-article__body u-pos-relative"><div class="annotator-wrapper">
              
  <aside class="s-article__sidebar">
              </aside>

  
        
  
        <div class="s-visual-article__body o-container c-sec  [ u-ptserif ]" id="">
      <p style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">In this episode of </span></span></span></span></span></span><em style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">The Horn</span></span></span></span></span></span></em><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">, Alan hosts a roundtable discussion with Dr Solomon Ayele Dersso, founder of Amani Africa, Paul-Simon Handy of the Institute for Security Studies, and Crisis Group expert Liesl Louw-Vaudran to discuss the state of peace and security in Africa. They assess the African Union’s response to the recent string of coups in West Africa and whether it still has the ability to deter military takeovers. They also talk about how the conflict in Sudan has tested the AU’s peace and security architecture and how competition between the AU and different regional bodies has hampered mediation efforts. Finally, they discuss what shape peacekeeping in Africa might take in the future and whether regional initiatives can fill the vacuum left by the departure of UN missions.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>

<script id="tweets" type="text/x-handlebars-template">
<div class='c-tweet-group c-slider__item c-slider__item--in-the-news'>
  {{#each tweets as |tweet|}}
    <div class='c-tweet [ u-df u-flexdc ] js-tweet'>
      <div class='c-tweet_user u-df u-aifs'>
        
  <div class='c-tweet__avatar u-br50p u-mar-r10 u-ofh'>
    <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}' target='_blank'>
      <img class='u-width-100' src='{{ tweet.user.profile_image_url }}' alt=''>
    </a>
  </div>
        <div class='u-df u-flexww'>
          <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}' class='c-tweet__name u-mar-r5' target='_blank'>{{ tweet.user.name }}</a>
          {{#if tweet.user.verified }}
            <span class='o-icon o-icon--inline u-mar-r5'><svg><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-verified'></use></svg></span>
          {{/if}}
          <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}' class='c-tweet__username u-gray--light' target='_blank'>@{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}</a>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class='c-tweet__content u-fg-1'>
        <div class='c-tweet__text u-mar-t10 u-ptserif u-fs21 u-gray u-wb'>
          {{{ tweet.text }}}
        </div>

        {{#if tweet.media }}
          <div class='c-tweet__img u-mar-t20'>
            <a href='{{ tweet.media.display_url}}' target='_blank'>
              <img class='u-width-100' src='{{ tweet.media.media_url}}:small' alt=''>
            </a>
          </div>
        {{/if}}

      </div>

      <div class='c-tweet__meta u-df u-aic u-jcsb u-mar-t20'>
        <div class='c-tweet__actions u-dif'>
          <div class='c-tweet__icon'><a href='https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?in_reply_to={{ tweet.id_str }}' class='o-icon o-icon--inline js-tweet-action' target='_blank'><svg class='u-gray--primary'><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-reply'></use></svg></a></div>
          <div class='c-tweet__icon u-mar-l20'><a href='https://twitter.com/intent/retweet?tweet_id={{ tweet.id_str }}' class='o-icon o-icon--inline js-tweet-action' target='_blank'><svg class='u-gray--primary'><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-retweet'></use></svg></a></div>
          <div class='c-tweet__icon u-mar-l20'><a href='https://twitter.com/intent/like?tweet_id={{ tweet.id_str }}' class='o-icon o-icon--inline js-tweet-action' target='_blank'><svg class='u-gray--primary'><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-like'></use></svg></a></div>
        </div>

        <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}/status/{{ tweet.id_str }}' class='c-tweet__timestamp u-fr u-fs13 u-gray--primary' target='_blank'>{{ tweet.created_at }}</a>
      </div>
    </div>
  {{/each}}
  </div>
</script>
  
<script id="tweet" type="text/x-handlebars-template">
<div class='c-tweet [ u-df u-flexdc ] js-tweet'>
    <div class='c-tweet_user u-df u-aifs'>
      
    <div class='c-tweet__avatar u-br50p u-mar-r10 u-ofh'>
      <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}' target='_blank'>
        <img class='u-width-100' src='{{ tweet.user.profile_image_url }}' alt=''>
      </a>
    </div>
      <div class='u-df u-flexww'>
        <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}' class='c-tweet__name u-mar-r5' target='_blank'>{{ tweet.user.name }}</a>
        {{#if tweet.user.verified }}
          <span class='o-icon o-icon--inline u-mar-r5'><svg><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-verified'></use></svg></span>
        {{/if}}
        <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}' class='c-tweet__username u-gray--light' target='_blank'>@{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}</a>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class='c-tweet__content u-fg-1'>
      <div class='c-tweet__text u-mar-t10 u-ptserif u-fs21 u-gray u-wb'>
        {{{ tweet.text }}}
      </div>

      {{#if tweet.media }}
        <div class='c-tweet__img u-mar-t20'>
          <a href='{{ tweet.media.display_url}}' target='_blank'>
            <img class='u-width-100' src='{{ tweet.media.media_url}}:small' alt=''>
          </a>
        </div>
      {{/if}}

    </div>

    <div class='c-tweet__meta u-df u-aic u-jcsb u-mar-t20'>
      <div class='c-tweet__actions u-dif'>
        <div class='c-tweet__icon'><a href='https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?in_reply_to={{ tweet.id_str }}' class='o-icon o-icon--inline js-tweet-action' target='_blank'><svg class='u-gray--primary'><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-reply'></use></svg></a></div>
        <div class='c-tweet__icon u-mar-l20'><a href='https://twitter.com/intent/retweet?tweet_id={{ tweet.id_str }}' class='o-icon o-icon--inline js-tweet-action' target='_blank'><svg class='u-gray--primary'><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-retweet'></use></svg></a></div>
        <div class='c-tweet__icon u-mar-l20'><a href='https://twitter.com/intent/like?tweet_id={{ tweet.id_str }}' class='o-icon o-icon--inline js-tweet-action' target='_blank'><svg class='u-gray--primary'><use xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' xlink:href='#twitter-like'></use></svg></a></div>
      </div>

      <a href='https://twitter.com/{{ tweet.user.screen_name }}/status/{{ tweet.id_str }}' class='c-tweet__timestamp u-fr u-fs13 u-gray--primary' target='_blank'>{{ tweet.created_at }}</a>
    </div>
  </div>

</script>
<script id="slideshow" type="text/x-handlebars-template">
<div class="o-modal--slideshow u-pos-relative c-slider c-slideshow o-container js-slideshow js-slideshow--modal" data-title="{{title}}">

  <div class="c-slider__track c-slider__track--slideshow">
  {{#items}}
    <div class="c-slider__item c-slider__item--{{@index}} [ c-slider__item--slideshow u-ofh ]" data-iid="{{img.iid}}">
      <div class="[ u-pa u-dn u-db@m u-dn@l ] c-slideshow__image c-slideshow__image--medium" style="background-image: url({{ img.medium }});"></div>
      <div class="[ u-pa u-dn u-dn@m u-db@l ] c-slideshow__image c-slideshow__image--large"  style="background-image: url({{ img.large }});"></div>
      <picture class="u-z-100 u-pos-relative u-db u-dn@m">
        <!--[if IE 9]><video style="display: none;"><![endif]-->
        <source srcset="{{ img.large }}" media="(min-width: 1040px)">
        <source srcset="{{ img.medium }}" media="(min-width: 760px)">
        <source srcset="{{ img.small }}" media="(min-width: 0px)">

        <!--[if IE 9]></video><![endif]-->
        <img class="o-image--cover" src="{{img.medium}}" alt="">
      </picture>

      <div class="c-slideshow__text u-pos-relative [ u-mar-t20 u-mar-b40 u-z-200 ]">
        {{#if desc}}<div class="c-slideshow__text--desc [ u-fs15 u-ptserif u-fs15 ]">{{desc}}</div>{{/if}}
        {{#if slide_title}}<div class="c-slideshow__text--desc [ u-fs15 u-ptserif u-fs15 ]">{{slide_title}}</div>{{/if}}
        <div class="c-slideshow__text--meta [ u-fs15 u-franklin u-gray u-mar-t10 ]">{{meta}}</div>

        <aside class="c-slideshow__social [ u-mar-t20 ]">
          <a href="?iid={{img.iid}}#ss-{{../id}}-{{@index}}" class="js-share js-slideshow--facebook c-slideshow__social--facebook u-mar-r20" data-sharer="FB">
            <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#facebook"></use></svg></span>
          </a>
          <a href="?iid={{img.iid}}#ss-{{../id}}-{{@index}}" class="js-share js-slideshow--twitter c-slideshow__social--twitter" data-sharer="TW">
            <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#twitter"></use></svg></span>
          </a>
        </aside>
      </div>
    </div>
  {{/items}}
  </div>

  <footer class="c-slideshow__footer [ u-dn u-df@m u-pos-relative ]">
    <div class="c-slideshow__desc-texts u-pos-relative">
      <div class="c-slideshow__content">
        <div class="c-slideshow__content--desc [ u-fs15 u-ptserif ]">{{desc}}</div>
        <div class="c-slideshow__content--meta [ u-fs15 u-mar-t10 u-franklin u-gray ]">{{meta}}</div>
      </div>

      <aside class="js-slideshow__social c-slideshow__social">
        <a href="javascript:;" class="js-share js-slideshow--facebook-target c-slideshow__social--facebook u-mar-r30" data-sharer="FB">
          <span class="o-icon o-icon--md"><svg><use xlink:href="#facebook"></use></svg></span>
        </a>
        <a href="javascript:;" class="js-share js-slideshow--twitter-target c-slideshow__social--twitter" data-sharer="TW">
          <span class="o-icon o-icon--md"><svg><use xlink:href="#twitter"></use></svg></span>
        </a>
      </aside>
    </div>

    <aside class="js-slider-controls c-slider__controls c-slider__controls--slideshow [ u-franklin u-aic ]">
      <a href="javascript:;" class="c-slider__controls--left">
        <span class="o-icon o-icon--reverse-h"><svg><use xlink:href="#chevron-right"></use></svg></span>
      </a>
      <div class="js-slider__page">
        <span class="js-slider__page--numerator"></span>/<span>{{items.length}}</span>
      </div>
      <a href="javascript:;" class="c-slider__controls--right">
        <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#chevron-right"></use></svg></span>
      </a>
    </aside>
  </footer>

</div>
</script>
<script id="savedItems" type="text/x-handlebars-template">
 
    {{#items}}
      <article class="c-news-listing [ u-df u-flexdc u-flexdr@m ]" data-lang="{{ language }}" data-nid="{{ nid }}">

        {{#if image}}
        <div class="c-news-listing__img">
          <div class="o-ar-16x9 o-image o-image--cover">
            <a href="{{ url }}" class="u-link-block u-pos-absolute u-z-1 u-db"></a>
            <picture>
              <!--[if IE 9]><video style="display: none;"><![endif]-->
              <source srcset="{{ image }}" media="(min-width: 0px)">
              <!--[if IE 9]></video><![endif]-->
              <img class="" src="{{ image }}" alt="">
            </picture>
          </div>
        </div>
        {{/if}}

        <div class="c-news-listing__content [ u-df u-flexdc ]">
          <div class="c-news-listing__meta u-ttu">
            <a href="{{ type.url }}" title="{{ type.name }}"><strong>{{ type.name }}</strong></a>
            {{#if label}}
              / <a href="{{ label.url }}">{{ label.name }}</a>
            {{/if}}
            <time class="u-mar-l15">{{ date }}</time>
          </div>
          <h4 class="c-news-listing__title"><a href="{{ url }}">{{ title }}</a></h3>
          <div class="c-news-listing__description [ u-ptserif u-fsi u-paragraph-mar ]">
            {{{ excerpt }}}
          </div>

          {{#if translations}}
          <div class="c-news-listing__meta u-gray--light [ u-mar-t15 ]">
            <svg class="c-news-listing__icon"><use xlink:href="#globe"></use></svg>
            {{{ translations }}}
          </div>
          {{/if}}

          <ul class="c-news-listing__actions [ u-df u-flex-11a u-jcfe u-flexww u-flexdr u-lsnone u-pad-0 u-mar-0 u-mar-t20 ]">
            <li class="c-news-listing__action">
              <a href="javascript:;" title="Remove" class="o-btn o-btn--underline o-btn--icon js-save">
                <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#saved"></use></svg></span>
                <span class="o-label u-mar-l5 [ u-dif u-fs13 u-franklin u-fwn u-ttu u-black ]">Remove</span>
              </a>
            </li>
            <li class="c-news-listing__action u-pr">
              <a href="/{{ url }}" title="Share" class="o-btn o-btn--underline o-btn--icon js-tooltip-toggle">
                <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#share"></use></svg></span>
                <span class="o-label u-mar-l5 [ u-dif u-fs13 u-franklin u-fwn u-ttu u-black ]">Share</span>
              </a>

              <ul class="o-tooltip [ u-lsnone u-pad-0 u-mar-0 u-bg-gray--primary u-z-1 ] js-tooltip">
                <li class="o-tooltip__item">
                  <a href="{{ url }}" class="o-tooltip__link js-share" title="Facebook" data-sharer="FB">
                    <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#facebook"></use></svg></span>
                    <span class="[ u-pos-relative u-top-3neg ] [ u-franklin u-fs13 u-ttu ]">Facebook</span>
                  </a>
                </li>
                <li class="o-tooltip__item">
                  <a href=" {{ twitter_share }}" class="o-tooltip__link js-share" title="Twitter" data-sharer="TW">
                    <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#twitter"></use></svg></span>
                    <span class="[ u-pos-relative u-top-3neg ] [ u-franklin u-fs13 u-ttu ]">Twitter</span>
                  </a>
                </li>
                <li class="o-tooltip__item">
                  <a href="{{ mailto_link }}" class="o-tooltip__link" title="Email">
                    <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#mail"></use></svg></span>
                    <span class="[ u-pos-relative u-top-3neg ] [ u-franklin u-fs13 u-ttu ]">Email</span>
                  </a>
                </li>
              </ul>
            </li>

            {{#if multiple_attachment}}
            <li class="c-news-listing__action">
              <a href="javascript:;" title="Download {{ documents.caption }}" class="o-btn o-btn--underline o-btn--icon js-multi-download" data-modal="{{ download_fid }}" data-modal-size="small" data-modal-color="gray">
                <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#download"></use></svg></span>
                <span class="o-label u-mar-l5 [ u-dif u-fs13 u-franklin u-fwn u-ttu u-black ]">Download full report</span>
              </a>

              <aside class="js-modal o-modal [ u-z-700 u-flexdc u-pf u-centered--v u-centered--h ] u-dn-imp u-ofs u-pad-b20 o-modal--small u-bg-gray--primary" data-modal-value="{{ download_fid }}">
                <header class="o-modal__header u-df">
                  <a href="javascript:;" class="js-modal-toggle o-modal__close">
                    <span class="o-icon">
                      <svg><use xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="#close"></use></svg>
                    </span>
                  </a>
                </header>
                <div class="o-modal__content">
                  <div class="[ u-pad-l30 u-pad-r30 u-pad-l70@m u-pad-r70@m u-mar-b10 ]">
                      <div class="u-franklin u-fs21 u-fs28@m u-fwb u-mar-b20@m">Download Full Report</div>
                      <div class="u-franklin u-fs15 u-fs18@m">Select your download language</div>
                    </div>
                  <ul class="u-lsnone u-franklin [ u-pad-0 u-mar-0 ]">
                    {{#each documents as |value key|}}
                    <li class="o-dropdown__item">
                      <a href="{{ value.link }}" type="{{ value.type }}" class="[ u-df u-jcfs u-aic u-width-100 ] [ u-pad-t15 u-pad-b15 u-pad-l30 u-pad-r30 u-pad-l70@m u-pad-r70@m ]" target="_blank" onclick="App.gaEvent.onClick(this);" data-ga-label="PDF Download Btn | {{ value.langcode }} | {{ ../title }}">
                        <span class="au-tal u-fs15 u-wbbw">{{ value.language }}</span>
                      </a>
                    </li>
                    {{/each}}
                  </ul>
                </div>
              </aside>
            </li>
            {{/if}}

            {{#if one_attachment}}
            <li class="c-news-listing__action">
              {{#each documents as |value key|}}
              <a href="{{ value.link }}" title="Download {{#if value.caption}}{{ value.caption }}{{/if}}" class="o-btn o-btn--underline o-btn--icon" target="_blank">
                <span class="o-icon"><svg><use xlink:href="#download"></use></svg></span>
                <span class="o-label u-mar-l5 [ u-dif u-fs13 u-franklin u-fwn u-ttu u-black ]">Download</span>
                {{#if value.langcode}}
                  <span class="[ u-franklin u-gray--light u-fs13 u-ttu u-mar-l5 ]">({{ value.langcode }})</span>
                {{/if}}
              </a>
              {{/each}}
            </li>
            {{/if}}

          </ul>
        </div>

      </article>
    {{/items}}
    
</script>

<script id="topicTimelines" type="text/x-handlebars-template">

    {{#items}}
      <div class="c-slider__item c-slider__item--timeline">
        <div class="u-pad-t20 u-width-100">
          <div class="u-fs12 u-ttu u-gray u-pad-b20">{{ posted_date }}</div>

          {{#if thumbnail}}
            <div class="o-ar-16x9 o-image o-image--cover">
              <a href="{{ url }}" class="u-pos-absolute u-link-block" title="{{ title }}"></a>
              <img src="{{ thumbnail }}"/>
            </div>
          {{/if}}

          {{#if publication_type}}
            <div class="c-news-listing__meta u-ttu">
              <a href="{{ publication_type.url }}" title="{{ publication_type.title }}">
                <strong>{{ publication_type.title }}</strong>
              </a>
              {{#if article_label}}
                / <a href="{{ article_label.url }}">{{ article_label.title }}</a>
              {{/if}}
              <time class="u-mar-l30" datetime="{{ posted_date_short }}">{{ posted_date }}</time>
            </div>
          {{/if}}

          <h4 class="c-news-listing__title">
            <a href="{{ url }}">{{ title }}</a>
          </h4>

          {{#if description}}
            <div class="c-news-listing__description [ u-ptserif u-fsi u-paragraph-mar u-ellipsis-3 ] js-ellipsis">{{{ description }}}</div>
          {{/if}}

        </div>
      </div>
    {{/items}}
  
</script>
<script id="video" type="text/x-handlebars-template">
  {{{ video }}}
</script>

  "content_text": "In this episode of\nThe Horn\n, Alan hosts a roundtable discussion with Dr Solomon Ayele Dersso, founder of Amani Africa, Paul-Simon Handy of the Institute for Security Studies, and Crisis Group expert Liesl Louw-Vaudran to discuss the state of peace and security in Africa. They assess the African Union’s response to the recent string of coups in West Africa and whether it still has the ability to deter military takeovers. They also talk about how the conflict in Sudan has tested the AU’s peace and security architecture and how competition between the AU and different regional bodies has hampered mediation efforts.             <h1 class="postTitle">
                <a id="cb_post_title_url" class="postTitle2 vertical-middle" href="https://www.cnblogs.com/cmt/p/19316348" title="发布于 2025-12-09 08:56">
    

    <span role="heading" aria-level="2">感谢艾思科蓝成为博客园赞助商</span>
    

</a>

            </h1>
            <div class="clear"></div>
            <div class="postBody">
                    <div id="cnblogs_post_description" style="display: none">
        
        在2025年岁末临近之际，园子又添惊喜，迎来一家新的赞助商——艾思科蓝。非常感谢艾思科蓝的赞助！以下是艾思科蓝的介绍：艾思科蓝(Aischolar)一站式科研学术服务数字化平台，致力于在学术交流、科研服务、科研教育、产学研协同领域为客户提供全过程数字化、智能化解决方案与服务，推进科研服务行业数字化转型升级，构建一流科研学术服务生态圈
    </div>
<div id="cnblogs_post_body" class="blogpost-body cnblogs-markdown">
<p>在2025年岁末临近之际，园子又添惊喜，迎来一家新的赞助商——<a href="https://ais.cn/u/QjqYJr" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">艾思科蓝</a>。</p>
<p>非常感谢艾思科蓝的赞助！</p>
<p>以下是艾思科蓝的介绍：</p>
<p><a href="https://ais.cn/u/QjqYJr" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">艾思科蓝</a>(AiScholar)，立足科研领域的连接者，致力于探索“人工智能+科研学术”的深度结合，打造 Al for Science 的科研服务新范式，在学术交流、科研论文、机构科研提升、成果转化等领域为客户提供全过程数字化、智能化解决方案与专业服务，推进科研服务行业数字化转型升级，构建一流科研学术服务生态圈。</p>
<p><a href="https://ais.cn/u/QjqYJr" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">艾思科蓝(AiScholar)</a>，为全球科研工作者和科研机构打造一站式科研学术服务数字化和智能化平台，链接全球高校、科研院所及学术机构的高端学术资源，实现科研学术创新成果的输出、传播与转化。通过自主研发构建起覆盖科研全生命周期的智能化矩阵，包括期刊大数据智能匹配系统、全过程<a href="https://ais.cn/u/VZZZJj" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">学术会议</a>数字化解决方案、AI同行审稿人系统、全球智库平台、成果转化与技术交易系统、艾思共享实验室平台、AI科研工作台、AI学术翻译与高级润色等具有行业创新性的系统和应用，助力基础研究，服务科技创新。</p>
<p><img src="https://img2024.cnblogs.com/blog/35695/202601/35695-20260108175333180-992084368.jpg" alt="" width="600" loading="lazy"></p>
<h4 id="国际学术会议">国际<a href="https://ais.cn/u/VZZZJj" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">学术会议</a></h4>
<p>面向有学术会议交流、学术合作、学术出版需求的客户和机构，以数字化技术为支撑，提供全过程学术会议数字化解决方案，深度赋能会议全流程运营和管理，支持全学科领域和跨学科交叉，使会议更为便捷、高效、专业，提升国际学术交流、学术出版效率，让学术交流更简单。</p>
<p><img src="https://img2024.cnblogs.com/blog/35695/202601/35695-20260108175527545-1207825159.jpg" alt="" width="600" loading="lazy"></p>
<h4 id="科研论文">科研论文</h4>
<p>面向<a href="https://ais.cn/u/VZZZJj" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">论文发表</a>需求客户提供的综合性解决方案，以智能化技术赋能公正高效同行审稿和期刊匹配推荐，由资深编辑团队和智库专家提供专业化的编译及发表支持服务，提高发表效率和录用率，助力基础研究。</p>
<p><img src="https://img2024.cnblogs.com/blog/35695/202601/35695-20260108175647631-827443426.jpg" alt="" width="600" loading="lazy"></p>
<h4 id="艾思编译">艾思编译</h4>
<p>全球高水平学者和母语专家，为您的文稿提供专业而准确的服务。<a href="https://ais.cn/u/QjqYJr" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">艾思编译</a>汇聚了生物医学、工程学科、计算机科学、人文社科、经管五大类主学科的1300+门细分领域专家以及大量跨学科专家， 为您的稿件匹配合适的专业大牛，提高录用率。</p>
<p><img src="https://img2024.cnblogs.com/blog/35695/202601/35695-20260108175830935-1183523564.jpg" alt="" width="600" loading="lazy"></p>
<p><img src="https://img2024.cnblogs.com/blog/35695/202601/35695-20260108175851544-1166682144.jpg" alt="" width="600" loading="lazy"></p>
<h4 id="学术头条"><a href="https://ais.cn/u/QjqYJr" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">学术头条</a></h4>
<p>面向全球高等院校、科研院所及科技企业科研工作者的科研咨讯与学术推广平台，通过构建图文、短视频、直播等融媒体矩阵，聚焦优质学术资源的传播与共享，专家学者研究成果的推广，弘扬科学家精神，提升学术影响力。</p>
<p><img src="https://img2024.cnblogs.com/blog/35695/202601/35695-20260108175958485-909133499.jpg" alt="" width="600" loading="lazy"></p>

点评：页面存在可见的 #post-date 时间（2025-12-09 08:56），系统按「页面可见即抽取」填入；标注对该站公告页不标时间（同型共 7 页）。争议点在标注规范本身——已登记为口径挂起项：不修标注凑分，也不为此改策略。

08 · Residual Cases & Shortcomings

残留失分案例、优化方向与整体不足

类别实例现状优化方向
test 拒识 0.125gmw 图集页 8 页仅正确拒识 1 页v9 合成标定样本未覆盖 gmw 模板族；评测纪律禁止读取 test 调优，如实登记扩充拒识标定的模板族覆盖；拒识信号从「图说性」向「正文文本熵」泛化
任务定义差异ISPRAS 17 页英文门户首页；president_go_kr 真图集页本系统按列表页规范拒识，ISPRAS 计为抽取对象——口径分歧而非错误（实例见 §07 样例 5）交付时声明口径；或拒识同时输出尽力而为的字段（双轨）
标注口径差异更新时间 50 页元数据含 dateModified 而不标；真实人名误填；时区与 12 小时制与 dev 标注口径不一致，无法同时满足制定统一口径文档；按下游用途声明采用口径
误填风险区14 页标注为空但页面有可见日期填入即构成误填（gov_cn、qstheory 已有先例），保持不填下游确有需要时提供「宽松模式」开关
段落级正文取舍oup 页面 15K 字碎正文壳、thenewshawks 正文漏抓（实例见 §07 样例 4）容器级方法无解（v13 负结果）训练方案路线 A（分类头块级模型，§06）
dev 口径挂起项cnblogs 标题 3 页、时间字段 7 页、用户名 1 页（实例见 §07 样例 6）边界分歧，登记未动与标注方对齐口径后一次性解除

整体不足（诚实清单）

  1. 评测：test 仅 28 页且站点族单一（拒识缺口直到终测才暴露）；ISPRAS 与自建标注的口径差异无正式对齐文档，外部基准上的绝对分受口径压制；缺少人工主观质量抽检环节（指标全对不代表可读）。
  2. 指标：误填与漏填同权计分，而生产上前者代价通常更高；标题精确匹配对大小写、标点变体过苛（title_sim 仅作诊断不计分）；正文 3-gram F1 对「多一句少一句」敏感，无法区分「模板噪声混入」与「同义改写」。
  3. 数据：dev 通用子集偏重中文门户，英文、小语种与政府站点偏薄——v11–v15 的英文策略增量实际由 ISPRAS 驱动发现，dev 无法独立暴露这些问题；口径挂起机制依赖人工登记，已累积 11 项未解。
  4. 策略：规则库的内容管理系统签名（容器先验、媒体名表）随模板演进而腐化，需要维护周期；正文字段依赖 trafilatura 黑盒；拒识判定对「正文极短的真实新闻」存在理论上的误拒面。
  5. 迭代闭环：模型补全层参与的全量重评需 2–5 分钟，迭代后半段成为节奏瓶颈；合成标定（v9）被证明可被模板覆盖不足骗过——标定集本身也需要版本化与扩充流程；探针脚本为一次性产物，未沉淀为通用的失分分析台。
  6. 人工参与：人工仅出现在标注与口径挂起登记两处；缺少「按不确定性采样送人工复核」的常态化队列——输出核验链能防止编造，但不能判断口径正误。
  7. 上下游：上游未覆盖渲染（空壳页已标记 needs_render 但无无头浏览器渲染环节）、反爬与增量抓取；下游未定义字段消费者契约（作者角色粒度、更新时间的业务语义、拒识页的双轨输出）——这些契约反过来决定误填与漏填的真实代价权重。
09 · Appendix: Iteration Log

附录：迭代全流程记录

每轮迭代对应一个 git 提交：目标问题 → 探针定位 → 策略增量 → 全量重评与逐页差异比对 → 指标写入提交信息。出现回归即修复或整体回滚，全程留痕可溯。指标曲线见 §04，环路设计见 §03。

v108a0bd30
模型补全层上线模型
目标问题：dev 集已趋于饱和，模型补全的价值须在外部基准上验证（ISPRAS 发布时间仅 0.292）。
  • 触发门控：标题缺失或来源过弱、作者为空、发布时间为空，且遵守规则层终判——满足其一才调用本地 Qwen2.5-7B，单页单次合并抽取
  • 三重输出核验：①值必须在页面文本中实际出现 ②署名须位于独立署名行并通过过滤链 ③时间须可解析——模型只能「定位与摘录」，无法编造页面上不存在的值
  • 同轮三项修正：规则层终判向模型层贯通、媒体名称过滤（「观察者网」）、敬称过滤（「朱先生」系报道提及人物而非署名）

英文垃圾署名过滤与欧式日期解析规则核验链

  • 垃圾署名三分过滤：社媒词与月份词一律拒收；机构/角色词须有页面可见的独立署名行佐证（「可见署名即真值」口径）

正文模型选容器实验【已回滚】负结果
实验假设：正文过短（<300 字）或臃肿（>6000 字）即视为抽取失败，由模型指定正文容器修复。
  • 假设被证伪：gov_ai 两页为 242/330 字的真实短讯（原得分 1.00/0.85），扩写后反降至 0.18/0.22——「短即失败」前提不成立；全程 0 正收益、2 页负收益，代码旁路留档
  • 回退前真实指标：ISPRAS 正文 0.761→0.752（其余字段持平，dev 聚合持平）——负结果如实入曲线（§04 三角标记点）
  • 附带收益：字段级触发门控细分，ISPRAS 单轮耗时 309 秒→132 秒
整体回滚至 v12 行为 · 段落级取舍问题移交训练方案（§06）

标题字段专项③：正文主标题优先规则模型裁决负结果
目标问题：约 21 页 og:title 与标注采用的正文主标题（h1）不一致。先尝试模型二选一裁决——模型偏好 og 侧短标题，与标注口径不符，遂改为确定性规则。
  • 元数据标题与 h1 互不包含时 h1 优先；双重守卫：h1 须位于正文语义区（防止博客标语误翻转）+ 栏目词与数字标签拒收（Welcome、Vol 65 No 6 等）
